content.text: RÃºssi (Icelandic for 'Russian') is a unique and strategic two-player variation of Whist played in Iceland. It distinguishes itself from standard 'Russian Whist' (Vint) by its hybrid layout: players have cards in their hand AND a collection of face-up and face-down cards on the table. It is a game of information asymmetry, where winning depends on managing visible threats and uncovering your own hidden resources.
Likely derived from Scandinavian Whist variants that were imported to Iceland in the late 19th/early 20th century. The name 'RÃºssi' is somewhat mysterious but common in Icelandic folk games.

Two players only. A standard 52-card pack is used; cards in each suit rank A (high) down to 2 (low). Turn to deal alternates; each player receives 26 cards: 9 face down on the table, 9 face up on those, and 8 in hand.
